name: Singapore Residential Tenancy Playbook (Tenant-Protective)
disclaimer: PORTFOLIO DEMO ONLY — NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Rules and statutory references must be reviewed by a Singapore-qualified Advocate & Solicitor before reliance.

rules.title: Stamp Duty Responsibility & 14-Day Stamping Window
rules.target_position: Contract explicitly states who bears Stamp Duty (customarily Tenant) and requires stamping via IRAS within 14 days of execution in Singapore (or 30 days if signed overseas).
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Clause is completely missing, waives stamping, or imposes penalties blocking IRAS stamping.
rules.statute_reference: Stamp Duties Act 1929 (Cap. 312), s. 15 & s. 52 (unstamped instruments inadmissible in court)

rules.title: Statutory Minimum Stay & URA/HDB Occupancy Caps
rules.target_position: Lease term is at least 3 consecutive months for private residential properties (or at least 6 months for HDB flats), and maximum unrelated occupants do not exceed 6 (or 8 for larger approved properties).
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Lease term under 3 months for private property, under 6 months for HDB, or permits unlawful short-term/subletting occupancy.
rules.statute_reference: Planning Act 1998 (URA Minimum Stay Rules) / Housing and Development Act 1959

rules.title: Prohibition on Unilateral Lockout or Seizure of Goods
rules.target_position: Landlord remedies for rent arrears require formal written notice, cure period (minimum 7–14 days), and due legal process without unilateral lockouts or seizing tenant property.
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Authorizes Landlord to forcibly enter, change locks, cut utilities, or seize/sell Tenant belongings without a court writ of distress.
rules.statute_reference: Distress Act 1934 (s. 4–5) & Conveyancing and Law of Property Act 1886

rules.title: Security Deposit Cap & Refund Timeline
rules.target_position: Security deposit is capped at 1 month rent for a 1-year lease (or 2 months for a 2-year lease) and refundable interest-free within 14 days of handover, minus itemized repair deductions.
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Deposit exceeds 2 months rent, allows arbitrary forfeiture for fair wear and tear, or omits a clear refund timeline.
rules.statute_reference: CEA Standard Tenancy Template Practice / Common Law Fair Wear & Tear

rules.title: Minor Repair Liability Cap
rules.target_position: Tenant liability for minor repairs is capped at S$150 to S$200 per item/incident, with structural, plumbing, and major appliance replacements borne by Landlord.
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Unlimited repair liability on Tenant, cap exceeding S$250 per item, or shifting structural/aircon compressor replacement onto Tenant.

rules.title: Diplomatic / Early Termination Clause (For Leases >= 24 Months)
rules.target_position: For leases of 24 months or longer, Tenant may terminate after 12 months by giving 2 months notice (or rent in lieu) if transferred out of Singapore or ceasing employment.
rules.unacceptable_triggers: 2-year lease omits a diplomatic clause entirely or requires Tenant to pay the full remaining lease balance upon relocation.
rules.statute_reference: Singapore Residential Leasing Market Standard (CEA Guidelines)

rules.title: PDPA Compliance for Tenant NRIC/FIN & Personal Data
rules.target_position: Landlord and agents collect, use, and retain Tenant/occupant personal data strictly for tenancy administration and statutory reporting in compliance with PDPA.
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Grants Landlord broad rights to share or sell Tenant personal data to third-party marketers.
rules.statute_reference: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA), s. 13 & s. 24

rules.title: Singapore Governing Law & Small Claims Tribunals Compatibility
rules.target_position: Agreement is governed by the laws of the Republic of Singapore and submits to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of Singapore Courts (preserving Small Claims Tribunals eligibility for leases <= 2 years).
rules.unacceptable_triggers: Foreign governing law or exclusive high-cost arbitration clauses that strip Small Claims Tribunals access.
rules.statute_reference: Small Claims Tribunals Act 1984 (s. 5 — residential leases up to 2 years)
